response: Assessing joint line positions by means of the contralateral knee is a new approach for planning knee revision surgery. This method involves using radiographs of the contralateral knee to assess the joint line position. The most precise parameter for this assessment is the distance between the fibular head and the joint line. This approach is advantageous as it corresponds to the tibia-first technique in revision surgery, and its accuracy is not influenced by factors such as the level of arthritis, age, gender, visibility of landmarks, or misalignment. This method provides a reliable and accurate way to assess joint line positions, which is essential for planning knee revision surgery.
